answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. Only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task is the slash triggered. Like a comet streaking across the sky, a single incorrect vote can expose a malicious identity. In a secure lagoon, identities must work together, not against each other. A well-designed system should have a secure vault to store and manage these bonds, ensuring the integrity of the network.
